false_positive_definition: A false positive is an omission finding for a field supported by the quoted source span and PR context, regardless of heading/label syntax. A missed completeness finding is a manually absent field not reported. Compare actual findings against these expectations; stale-evidence warnings are assessed separately.
limits: Nine live public body snapshots are a convenience sample, not a population rate or measured time saving.
Presence does not verify behavior, execution, linked content, video, hardware, accepted-issue status or artifact accessibility.
Legacy/draft/external findings remain nonblocking. Full author fingerprints require 40 hexadecimal characters; metadata head alone is not author evidence.
Prior zero-FP counts used label-restricted expectations and were invalid; retained red logs demonstrate the omissions.

The later 46-present/26-absent classification also wrongly excluded #1209 qualitative check/results; the panel-settled correction is 47 present/25 absent, not evidence of global accuracy or collection-order independence.
